passage:
Before the middle of the fifteenth century, books in Europe were copied by hand. This work was slow and expensive, and a single book could take a scribe many months to complete. As a result, books were rare, and only wealthy people, religious institutions, and universities could own them. This situation changed dramatically when Johannes Gutenberg introduced a printing press that used movable metal type around 1440. With this machine, a printer could produce hundreds of identical pages in the time it once took to copy a single one.

The effects of the printing press were enormous. Books became cheaper and far more common, and literacy began to spread beyond the small group of educated elites. Ideas could now travel quickly across cities and countries. Scholars in different regions were able to read the same texts and build on one another's work. Many historians argue that the printing press helped make possible later movements such as the Reformation and the Scientific Revolution, because these movements depended on the rapid sharing of new and sometimes controversial ideas.

questions.question: What is the main idea of the passage?

options.A: Gutenberg was the richest man in Europe
options.B: The printing press made books cheaper and helped ideas spread widely
options.C: Books copied by hand were more beautiful than printed books
options.D: Universities were the only places that owned books

questions.explanation: The passage focuses on how the printing press lowered the cost of books and allowed ideas and literacy to spread. This is the main idea.

questions.question: According to the passage, why were books rare before the printing press?

options.A: Few people wanted to read them
options.B: There was not enough paper in Europe
options.C: Copying them by hand was slow and expensive
options.D: Governments did not allow people to own books

questions.explanation: The passage states that copying books by hand 'was slow and expensive', which made books rare.

questions.question: The word 'dramatically' in the passage is closest in meaning to
questions.explanation: 'This situation changed dramatically' means the situation changed greatly or to a large degree. 'Greatly' is the closest meaning.

questions.question: What can be inferred about the spread of new ideas after the printing press?

options.B: It was limited to religious texts only
options.C: It was made easier by cheaper, more available books
options.D: It stopped completely during the Reformation

questions.explanation: Since books became cheaper and more common and 'ideas could now travel quickly', it can be inferred that the spread of ideas was made easier by more available books.

questions.question: The phrase 'this machine' in the passage refers to
questions.explanation: 'With this machine, a printer could produce hundreds of identical pages' refers to the printing press that Gutenberg introduced.

passage:
Coral reefs are among the most diverse ecosystems on Earth. Although they cover less than one percent of the ocean floor, they provide a home for about a quarter of all marine species. A coral reef is built by tiny animals called coral polyps, which produce a hard outer skeleton of calcium carbonate. Over thousands of years, the skeletons of countless polyps accumulate to form the large structures that we recognize as reefs.

Coral polyps have an unusual relationship with tiny algae that live inside their tissues. The algae use sunlight to make food and share some of it with the coral, while the coral gives the algae shelter and important nutrients. This partnership benefits both organisms. However, it is also fragile. When ocean water becomes too warm, the coral expels the algae, and the reef loses its main source of food and its bright color. This event, known as coral bleaching, can cause large areas of reef to die. Because rising ocean temperatures are now more frequent, scientists warn that many reefs around the world are in serious danger.

questions.question: What is the passage mainly about?

options.A: How tourists can visit coral reefs safely
options.B: How coral reefs form and why they are at risk
options.C: Why algae are dangerous to the ocean
options.D: How calcium carbonate is used by humans

questions.explanation: The passage explains how reefs are built by polyps and why warming oceans threaten them through bleaching. This is the main idea.

questions.question: According to the passage, what do the algae provide for the coral?
questions.explanation: The passage states that 'the algae use sunlight to make food and share some of it with the coral'.

questions.question: The word 'fragile' in the passage is closest in meaning to
questions.explanation: The partnership is called 'fragile' because warm water can easily break it. 'Easily damaged' is the closest meaning.

questions.question: What can be inferred about coral bleaching from the passage?

options.B: It is caused mainly by tourists
options.C: It is likely to increase as ocean temperatures rise
options.D: It has no effect on marine species

questions.explanation: Because bleaching happens when water is too warm and 'rising ocean temperatures are now more frequent', it can be inferred that bleaching is likely to increase.

passage:
For many years, people thought of sleep simply as a period of rest, a time when the body and brain shut down. Recent research, however, suggests that the sleeping brain is surprisingly active and that sleep plays an essential role in learning and memory. During the day, the brain takes in a huge amount of information. During sleep, it appears to sort through this information, strengthening important memories and discarding details that are not needed.

Scientists have observed that people who sleep well after studying tend to remember new material better than those who stay awake. In several experiments, students who learned a task and then slept performed more accurately the next day than students who learned the same task but were kept awake. Researchers believe that certain stages of sleep help move information from short-term storage into more permanent memory. These findings have practical consequences. They suggest that students who sacrifice sleep in order to study longer may actually harm their performance, because the brain needs sleep to organize and store what has been learned.

questions.question: What is the main idea of the passage?

options.A: Students should never study at night
options.B: Sleep is a period when the brain does nothing
options.C: Sleep plays an important role in learning and memory
options.D: Memory has no connection to the brain

questions.explanation: The passage argues that sleep is active and helps the brain store memories. This is the main idea.

questions.question: According to the passage, what did students who slept after studying do compared with those who stayed awake?

options.C: They studied for a longer time

questions.explanation: The passage states that students who slept 'performed more accurately the next day' than those who were kept awake.

questions.question: What can be inferred about students who give up sleep to study longer?

options.A: They will always get higher scores
options.B: They may reduce their ability to remember what they studied
options.C: They do not need to review the material
options.D: They learn faster than other students

questions.explanation: Since the brain needs sleep to store memories, it can be inferred that students who sacrifice sleep may reduce their ability to remember the material.

questions.question: The word 'discarding' in the passage is closest in meaning to
questions.explanation: The brain is described as 'discarding details that are not needed', meaning throwing them away. 'Throwing away' is the closest meaning.
